latest_quarter.label: Q2 2026 (Apr-Jun 2026; quarter ended Jun 28, 2026)
latest_quarter.operating_margin_basis: non-GAAP (applies to operating margin and EPS; gross margin is 59.8% on both bases). GAAP operating margin 32.9% ($437.8M); GAAP diluted EPS $2.38 vs non-GAAP $2.47 (consensus ~$2.06-2.09).

guidance: Q3 2026 (given Jul 28, 2026): revenue $1.20-1.30B; GAAP EPS $1.79-2.09; non-GAAP EPS $1.85-2.15; gross margin 58%-59%; non-GAAP operating margin 28%-30%. The midpoint was ~21% above the ~$1.03B consensus at the time. Management expects 2H 2026 growth over 1H in memory, auto/industrial, Integrated Systems Test, Product Test and Robotics, partly offset by mobile softness and compute order timing; it said in April that 1H would be 55%-60% of 2026 revenue. It expects 'renewed growth in 2027' (VIP compute next generation in early 2027; meaningful production share at a second cloud hyperscaler in 2027). Target model: ~$6B revenue and $9.50-11.00 non-GAAP EPS, 59%-61% gross margin, opex growth under half of revenue growth. Robotics: breakeven targeted for 2026 (Feb 2026 call) and expected to grow roughly in line with the company over the medium term. Street consensus for Q3 2026 (Yahoo): revenue $1.26B, EPS $2.05; Q4 2026: revenue $1.26B, EPS $2.02.

physical_ai_exposure.description: Teradyne Robotics (Universal Robots collaborative arms and MiR autonomous mobile robots) had Q2 2026 revenue of $100M (+33% YoY, +9% QoQ; 7.5% of revenue; CEO calls it 'about 10%'). Trend: Q2 2025 $74.9M, Q3 2025 $75M (UR $62M, MiR $13M; flat QoQ and down YoY), Q4 2025 $89M (+19% QoQ), Q1 2026 $91M (+32% YoY), Q2 2026 $100M, five straight quarters of growth. Electronics manufacturing/semiconductor (incl. data-center hardware assembly) became the largest and fastest-growing robotics end market (+50% QoQ in Q2 2026). U.S. sales were 32% of Robotics, and a U.S. robotics manufacturing center is due to open in late 2026. A marquee e-commerce logistics customer's revenue tripled from 2025 to 2026, and management expects it to 'triple again' in 2027. Products and partners: UR Gen 7 platform launched Sep 14, 2026 (CB7 controller with 40% more compute, PolyScope X with open APIs/ROS2, AI-ready tool flange, new g-Series arms); Sereact partnership (Oct 21, 2026) running Cortex AI on UR arms with NVIDIA Jetson Thor, Isaac Sim and Cosmos, with hundreds of UR dual-arm systems already shipped; strategic investment in Bright Machines (Oct 5, 2026) for robotic assembly of AI-infrastructure hardware; UR claims 100,000+ industrial deployments. The larger AI exposure is indirect: AI drove over 60% of Q2 2026 revenue through testing GPUs, custom AI accelerators, HBM/DRAM and networking chips.
physical_ai_exposure.optionality_notes: No analyst sum-of-the-parts valuing Robotics separately was found in the sources reviewed. Robotics is ~7.5% of revenue and has not been reported as profitable (breakeven targeted in 2026), so the ~$48B valuation rests mainly on AI-driven semiconductor test. Management calls physical AI 'probably the most important trend' for robotics over the next few years. Illustrative estimate (my assumption, not an analyst figure): at 2-4x LTM robotics sales (~$355M), Robotics would be worth ~$0.7-1.4B, or about 1.5%-3% of market cap.

cost_and_supply_chain_notes: Revenue is heavily Asia-weighted (Asia Pacific 87% in Q2 2026) because testers ship to OSAT and foundry test floors in Asia; Americas 8%, EMEA 5%. Robotics is building a U.S.-based manufacturing center (opening later in 2026), which reduces tariff exposure on U.S. robot sales (32% of Robotics revenue). Tariff costs were not quantified in the sources reviewed. Gross margin is mix-driven: 60.9% in Q1 2026, 59.8% in Q2, guided to 58%-59% for Q3 on product mix and new launches. Recent deals: MultiLane Test Products JV (75% controlling stake, $157.8M, Apr 8, 2026); Quantifi Photonics ($127.2M, May 31, 2025); Infineon ATE technology (EUR 17.6M, Jan 31, 2025); Technoprobe investment (amortization excluded from non-GAAP); agreed $300M strategic equity investment in FormFactor (October 2026, subject to approvals); undisclosed investment in Bright Machines (Oct 5, 2026). New products: Magnum E2 memory tester (Sep 29), Titan HP burn-in for AI data-center devices (Oct 6), UltraFLEXplus S for edge AI (Oct 12), Iris 100 for microLED.
debt_notes: No borrowings at Jun 28, 2026. The revolving credit facility had $200M drawn at Dec 31, 2025; in 1H 2026 Teradyne borrowed $350M and repaid $550M, leaving zero outstanding. Interest expense was $3.0M in Q2 2026 ($6.1M for 1H) vs $0.8M a year earlier. Facility size, rate basis and maturity were not found (revolvers are usually floating-rate, unverified). Aggregators list $100.1M of 'total debt', probably lease liabilities. Liquidity is thin relative to new commitments: $517M of cash and marketable securities vs the $300M FormFactor investment; Q2 2026 free cash flow was $378M ($579M in 1H). Q2 2026 capital return: $69M buybacks, $20M dividends ($0.13/quarter).
customer_concentration: High. In 2025 Teradyne had two customers above 10% of revenue as 'specifying' customers and one above 10% as a 'purchasing' customer, roughly 10% each (Q4 2025 call); the same three still exceeded 10% in Q1 2026. Compute (~70%-75% of SoC revenue) depends on a few AI chip programs: majority tester share at one cloud hyperscaler's custom XPU (dual-sourced since 2024), second-source qualification at a second hyperscaler (meaningful production share expected in 2027), and second-source status on a merchant GPU (initial part released early 2026 on a small tester fleet; ~$50M line of sight for 2026; goal of up to ~30% of that account's compute test over 3-5 years). Management says the segment is 'very concentrated, with only a few players driving significant ATE purchases' and has about 13 weeks of visibility.
key_drivers: AI compute test: compute revenue up nearly 600% YoY in Q2 2026; AI drove >60% of Q2 revenue (nearly 70% in Q1)

Hyperscaler custom-silicon wins: majority share at one hyperscaler, production share at a second from 2027; each opportunity worth 'hundreds of millions of dollars of TAM to $1 billion of TAM' per year
Memory: record $212M in Q2 2026 with book-to-bill above 2; 2026 memory test TAM seen >40% above 2025; HBM 2027 expected to keep growing, 'not going to be a digestion'

Rising test intensity: semi test ~8% of semiconductor capex in early 2026 vs ~4% in 2023; ATE market seen reaching $20B+ over time; co-packaged optics test TAM ~$100M in 2026 rising to $300-700M by 2028
Robotics recovery: +33% YoY in Q2 2026; data-center electronics and e-commerce logistics demand; UR Gen 7; physical-AI partners on NVIDIA platforms; breakeven targeted in 2026
Target model: ~$6B revenue and $9.50-11.00 non-GAAP EPS vs 2026 consensus $5.14B and $9.10; 2027 consensus $6.3B and $11.75
key_risks: Order lumpiness and short visibility (~13 weeks); compute is 1H-weighted in 2026 with the next VIP generation in early 2027, so 2H 2026 and early 2027 could dip
Customer concentration: three customers at ~10% each, plus heavy reliance on a few AI accelerator programs
Competition from the incumbent tester vendor on GPU and accelerator programs; share gains are gradual over 3-5 years
Extreme stock volatility: beta 1.75; 58 trading days with moves of 6% or more since Jan 2025; -36.7% from the 52-week high of $487.91
AI capex cycle risk: chip stocks sold off in October 2026 (TER -30.5% from Oct 5 to Oct 22)
Geopolitics: 87% of revenue from Asia Pacific; export controls and tariffs could hit tester shipments or robot costs
Robotics profitability: still around breakeven at best; cobot demand tied to industrial capex; restructuring costs ($16.9M in 1H 2025, $6.5M in 1H 2026)
Capital allocation: $300M FormFactor stake and other investments against $517M of cash
